scope: Frozen PPO policy diagnostic on in-flight training states; no learning or benchmark cases.
hypothesis: The GRU actor's carried memory changes future returns at the same physical state, while the stateless privileged critic cannot condition on that memory.
selection: Choose8 nonterminal source worlds aged at least1second with nonzero recurrent memory, evenly spaced in sorted episode age; do not select by outcome.
comparison: Actual stored actor memory versus zero actor memory; identical complete environment, objective history, weights, exploration scale and paired random action noise.
replicas: 16 paired stochastic continuations per state, implemented as two batches of8 replicas in the existing64-world environment.
budget: Each rollout runs until all worlds terminate or the original300second finite horizon. No parameter updates. Report actual active interactions and allocated slots.
decision: Consider a memory-conditioned critic only if at least2/8 states show absolute paired mean-return difference>0.2 with a descriptive paired95percent bootstrap interval excluding0. Otherwise reject this as a supported next intervention on this probe.
limitations: Clearing memory in flight is an intervention and may be outside natural history support. A positive result establishes sensitivity, not naturally occurring state aliasing or the sole collapse cause. Intervals are descriptive across8 probes.
reuse: Source state identity and probability/recurrence checks were already verified. Reuse their recorded evidence without source rehash or fixed-scene reevaluation.
